Recommended Gaming Resolutions:

  • 1920x1080
  • 2560x1440
  • 3840x2160
The GeForce RTX 5080 is an enthusiast-class graphics card by NVIDIA, launched on January 30th, 2025. Built on the 5 nm process, and based on the GB203 graphics processor, in its GB203-400-A1 variant, the card supports DirectX 12 Ultimate. This ensures that all modern games will run on GeForce RTX 5080. Additionally, the DirectX 12 Ultimate capability guarantees support for hardware-raytracing, variable-rate shading and more, in upcoming video games. The GB203 graphics processor is a large chip with a die area of 378 mm² and 45.6 billion transistors. It features 10752 shading units, 336 texture mapping units, and 112 ROPs. Also included are 336 Tensor Cores which help improve the speed of machine learning applications with support for the FP4, FP6, INT8 and FP8 data formats. The GPU also has 84 raytracing acceleration cores. NVIDIA has paired 16 GB GDDR7 memory with the GeForce RTX 5080, which is connected using a 256-bit memory interface. The GPU is operating at a frequency of 2295 MHz, which can be boosted up to 2617 MHz, memory is running at 1875 MHz (30 Gbps effective).
Being a dual-slot card, the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 draws power from 1x 16-pin power connector, with power draw rated at 360 W maximum. Display outputs include: 1x HDMI 2.1b, 3x DisplayPort 2.1b. GeForce RTX 5080 is connected to the rest of the system using a PCI-Express 5.0 x16 interface. The card's dimensions are 304 mm x 137 mm x 40 mm, and it features a dual-slot cooling solution. Its price at launch was 999 US Dollars.
